entities.name: Melioidosis
entities.description: Severe, life-threatening tropical infectious disease caused by the environmental Gram-negative bacterium Burkholderia pseudomallei, characterized by protean manifestations ranging from localized abscesses and severe cavitary pneumonia to fulminant bacteremic septic shock, especially in patients with diabetes mellitus.

entities.name: Burkholderia pseudomallei
entities.description: Aerobic, motile, oxidase-positive, Gram-negative saprophytic bacillus exhibiting a characteristic bipolar 'safety-pin' staining appearance; persists in tropical wet soil and water and possesses extensive intrinsic antimicrobial resistance.

entities.name: Acute Fulminant Septicemia
entities.description: Acute hyperacute bacteremic septicemia presenting with rapid hemodynamic collapse, high fevers, rigors, metabolic acidosis, and high early mortality.

entities.name: Acute Lobar Pneumonia
entities.description: Acute dense alveolar pulmonary consolidation with purulent sputum, pleuritic chest pain, and severe respiratory compromise.

entities.name: Subacute Cavitary Pneumonia
entities.description: Indolent or subacute necrotizing pneumonia presenting with prominent upper-lobe cavitary lesions, productive cough, hemoptysis, and night sweats.

entities.name: Suppurative Parotitis
entities.description: Acute bacterial inflammation and abscess formation of the parotid gland, representing a distinctive pediatric manifestation in Southeast Asia.

entities.name: Prostatic Abscess
entities.description: Suppurative focal infection of the prostate gland in adult males, presenting with perineal pain, dysuria, and urinary obstruction.

entities.name: Splenic Microabscesses
entities.description: Multiple small, discrete pyogenic collections scattered throughout the splenic red pulp due to hematogenous dissemination.

entities.name: Hepatic Microabscesses
entities.description: Multifocal discrete suppurative bacterial foci scattered throughout both lobes of the liver.

entities.name: Septic Arthritis
entities.description: Acute pyogenic infection of synovial joint spaces, predominantly targeting large weight-bearing joints.

entities.name: Acute Osteomyelitis
entities.description: Suppurative infection of bone cortex and marrow space leading to cortical erosion, subperiosteal abscesses, and sequestrum formation.

entities.name: Brainstem Encephalitis
entities.description: Inflammatory infection of the brainstem (rhombencephalitis) characteristic of neurological melioidosis.

entities.name: Cranial Nerve Palsies
entities.description: Acute focal neuropathies of cranial nerves, particularly unilateral or bilateral facial nerve (CN VII) and abducens nerve (CN VI).

entities.name: Flaccid Quadriparesis
entities.description: Acute lower motor neuron-like flaccid paralysis of all four extremities due to extensive myelitis or radiculoneuropathy.

entities.name: Cutaneous Pustules
entities.description: Disseminated discrete pustular skin eruptions with erythematous halos and central necrotic breakdown.

entities.name: Indolent Skin Ulcer
entities.description: Chronic non-healing cutaneous ulceration resulting from direct percutaneous bacterial inoculation.

entities.name: Subcutaneous Abscess
entities.description: Discrete soft-tissue fluctuant purulent collection located within subcutaneous fat and dermal tissues.

entities.name: Suppurative Lymphadenitis
entities.description: Acute pyogenic infection of regional lymph node chains causing marked adenomegaly, fluctuance, and periadenitis.

entities.name: Pericardial Effusion
entities.description: Exudative or purulent fluid accumulation within the pericardial sac causing cardiac compromise.

entities.name: Infective Endocarditis
entities.description: Endovascular vegetative infection of native or prosthetic cardiac valves causing bacteremia and embolization.

entities.name: Mycotic Aneurysm
entities.description: Infected arterial pseudoaneurysm caused by bacterial colonization of the arterial wall.

entities.name: Renal Cortical Abscess
entities.description: Focal suppurative collections within the renal cortex or medulla resulting from hematogenous bacteremic seeding.

entities.name: Epididymo-Orchitis
entities.description: Acute suppurative infection of the epididymis and testicle presenting with scrotal swelling and tenderness.

entities.name: Psoas Abscess
entities.description: Large retroperitoneal purulent collection within the belly of the psoas major muscle.

entities.name: Mediastinal Abscess
entities.description: Suppurative purulent phlegmon or encapsulated abscess within the anterior or posterior mediastinum.

entities.name: Pleural Empyema
entities.description: Macroscopically purulent, loculated fluid collection within the pleural space.

entities.name: Cerebral Abscess
entities.description: Discrete parenchymal brain abscess with ring enhancement and surrounding vasogenic edema.

entities.name: Necrotizing Fasciitis
entities.description: Rapidly progressive, life-threatening necrosis of subcutaneous tissues and deep muscular fascia.

entities.name: Thyroid Abscess
entities.description: Acute suppurative inflammation and liquefaction necrosis of the thyroid gland.

entities.name: Corneal Ulcer
entities.description: Suppurative keratitis and corneal stromal ulceration following ocular exposure to contaminated mud or water.

entities.name: Adrenal Abscess
entities.description: Suppurative necrosis of the adrenal gland causing focal abscess and adrenal crisis.

entities.name: Pancreatic Abscess
entities.description: Focal circumscribed collection of purulent material within or adjacent to the pancreatic parenchyma.

entities.name: Peritonitis
entities.description: Acute diffuse inflammation of the peritoneal lining resulting from microabscess rupture or dialysis catheter colonization.

entities.name: Septic Shock
entities.description: Severe sepsis complicated by persistent arterial hypotension refractory to volume resuscitation.

entities.name: Acute Bronchitis
entities.description: Primary superficial tracheobronchial inflammation presenting without parenchymal consolidation.

entities.name: Chronic Melioidosis
entities.description: Indolent clinical illness lasting greater than two months with chronic fever, wasting, and abscesses.

entities.name: Miliary Melioidosis
entities.description: Widespread diffuse hematogenous dissemination producing countless tiny micronodular lesions across multiple organs.

entities.name: Spinal Epidural Abscess
entities.description: Purulent collection within the spinal epidural space causing mechanical spinal cord or nerve root compression.

entities.name: Pyomyositis
entities.description: Primary acute bacterial suppurative infection within skeletal muscle bellies forming deep intramuscular abscesses.

entities.name: Mesenteric Lymphadenitis
entities.description: Suppurative bacterial inflammation of mesenteric lymph nodes causing lower abdominal quadrant pain.

entities.name: Deep Neck Abscess
entities.description: Complex suppurative infection of the parapharyngeal, retropharyngeal, or submandibular deep fascial planes.

entities.name: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation
entities.description: Systemic thrombohemorrhagic disorder characterized by widespread microvascular thrombosis and consumptive coagulopathy.

entities.name: Preauricular Parotid Swelling
entities.description: Tense, erythematous, painful swelling overlying the preauricular space and mandibular angle.

entities.name: Fluctuant Parotid Abscess
entities.description: Palpable fluid wave over the parotid gland with purulent secretion from Stensen duct orifice upon gentle palpation.

entities.name: Perineal Tenderness
entities.description: Exquisite focal pain elicited by deep palpation over the perineum and pelvic floor.

entities.name: Tender Fluctuant Prostate
entities.description: Extremely tender, boggy, warm, and distinctly fluctuant prostatic mass palpated on digital rectal examination.

entities.name: Acute Urinary Retention
entities.description: Sudden inability to micturate with a tense, painful, palpable suprapubic bladder dull to percussion.

entities.name: Ecthyma-Like Necrotic Pustules
entities.description: Crops of discrete pustules with central necrosis, violaceous borders, and black eschar-like crusts.

entities.name: Violaceous Undermined Ulcer
entities.description: Indolent skin ulceration displaying violaceous, rolled, or undermined margins with a purulent base.

entities.name: High Remittent Fever
entities.description: Severe body temperature elevation exceeding 39.5°C to 40°C with daily remissions not returning to baseline.

entities.name: Profound Rigors
entities.description: Violent, shaking chills with severe involuntary muscle contractions coinciding with bacteremic waves.

entities.name: Peripheral Facial Palsy
entities.description: Unilateral lower motor neuron facial weakness with loss of forehead wrinkling and inability to close the ipsilateral eye.

entities.name: Limb Flaccidity
entities.description: Profound hypotonia and absent deep tendon reflexes in the upper or lower extremities.

entities.name: Truncal Ataxia
entities.description: Inability to maintain steady upright posture with wide-based unsteady gait and midline titubation.

entities.name: Abducens Nerve Palsy
entities.description: Inability to abduct the affected eye causing horizontal diplopia on lateral gaze.

entities.name: Bulbar Dysphagia
entities.description: Impaired swallowing, absent gag reflex, nasal regurgitation, and pooling of oral secretions.

entities.name: Nuchal Rigidity
entities.description: Resistance to passive flexion of the neck accompanied by positive Kernig and Brudzinski signs.

entities.name: Joint Effusion
entities.description: Gross distension of a synovial joint cavity with palpable fluid wave, warmth, and erythema.

entities.name: Bony Point Tenderness
entities.description: Sharp, localized tenderness on direct percussion or firm palpation over bone cortices.

entities.name: Positive Psoas Sign
entities.description: Severe lower abdominal or retroperitoneal pain elicited by passive hyperextension of the hip.

entities.name: Costovertebral Angle Tenderness
entities.description: Acute pain elicited by gentle fist percussion over the twelfth rib and spine junction.

entities.name: Right Hypochondriac Tenderness
entities.description: Pain and involuntary muscular resistance on palpation below the right costal margin.

entities.name: Left Hypochondriac Tenderness
entities.description: Pain and localized muscular resistance on palpation over the left upper quadrant and spleen.

entities.name: Pleuritic Friction Rub
entities.description: Superficial raspy, grating sound auscultated over the thoracic wall synchronous with breathing.

entities.name: Tubular Breath Sounds
entities.description: High-pitched, loud, hollow bronchial auscultatory sounds over consolidated lung parenchyma.

entities.name: Tachypnea and Retractions
entities.description: Elevated respiratory rate (>30 breaths/min) accompanied by intercostal and supraclavicular retractions.

entities.name: Hyperdynamic Vasodilation
entities.description: Bounding peripheral pulses, warm flushed extremities, and flash capillary refill in early distributive shock.

entities.name: Mottled Cold Peripheries
entities.description: Cutaneous mottling, delayed capillary refill (>3 seconds), and cold clammy skin in decompensated shock.

entities.name: Petechial Purpura
entities.description: Non-blanching pinpoint petechiae and purpuric macules scattered over the skin and mucous membranes.

entities.name: Subcutaneous Emphysema
entities.description: Palpable crackling or crepitation within soft tissues caused by subcutaneous gas accumulation.

entities.name: Honeycomb Splenic Microabscesses
entities.description: Multiple small, discrete round hypoechoic or hypodense parenchymal lesions creating a honeycomb appearance on ultrasound or CT.

entities.name: Swiss-Cheese Hepatic Microabscesses
entities.description: Widespread discrete hypoechoic pyogenic microabscesses scattered throughout the liver resembling Swiss cheese.

entities.name: Prostatic Fluid Collections
entities.description: Discrete, thick-walled hypoechoic or anechoic cystic collections with posterior acoustic enhancement in the prostate.

entities.name: Upper Lobe Cavitation
entities.description: Dense alveolar consolidation with thin- or thick-walled cavitary lesions located predominantly in the upper lobes on CXR or CT.

entities.name: Diffuse Nodular Infiltrates
entities.description: Bilateral, diffuse multi-nodular alveolar opacities and patchy infiltrates signifying hematogenous septic dissemination.

entities.name: Absence of Hilar Adenopathy
entities.description: Upper-lobe consolidation and cavitation occurring without enlargement of mediastinal or hilar lymph nodes.

entities.name: Loculated Pleural Effusion
entities.description: Echogenic, multi-loculated fluid collections with fibrinous stranding and thickened pleural surfaces on thoracic POCUS.

entities.name: Pericardial Fluid Accumulation
entities.description: Anechoic fluid collection separating pericardial layers with fibrinous strands seen on focused cardiac ultrasound.

entities.name: Joint Space Distension
entities.description: Prominent anechoic or hypoechoic synovial fluid distension and hypervascular synovial thickening on POCUS.

entities.name: Subperiosteal Fluid Collection
entities.description: Cortical breach on plain radiographs with overlying anechoic subperiosteal purulent collection on ultrasound.

entities.name: T2 Brainstem Hyperintensity
entities.description: Abnormal hyperintense signal on T2 and FLAIR MRI sequences in the pons, medulla, and upper cervical cord.

entities.name: Ring-Enhancing Cerebral Lesions
entities.description: Discrete intracranial ring-enhancing nodules with central necrosis and surrounding vasogenic edema on contrast MRI.

entities.name: Psoas Rim-Enhancing Fluid
entities.description: Hypodense fluid collection with prominent peripheral rim enhancement expanding the psoas muscle belly on CT.

entities.name: Mediastinal Soft-Tissue Fullness
entities.description: Pathologic widening of the mediastinum or retrocardiac soft-tissue density on plain chest radiography.

entities.name: Marked Neutrophilic Leukocytosis
entities.description: Elevated white blood cell count (15,000 to 35,000/µL) dominated by mature and immature neutrophils.

entities.name: Prominent Toxic Bandemia
entities.description: Band neutrophil precursors exceeding 15% to 20% with toxic granulations and Döhle bodies on peripheral smear.

entities.name: Profound Leukopenia
entities.description: Paradoxical depletion of white blood cells (<3,000/µL) occurring during overwhelming endotoxemic septic shock.

entities.name: Severe Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Platelet count declining below 50,000 to 100,000/µL secondary to microvascular platelet consumption in DIC.

entities.name: Massive CRP Elevation
entities.description: Extreme elevation of serum C-reactive protein (>150 to 300 mg/L) indicating massive acute-phase response.

entities.name: Marked Procalcitonin Elevation
entities.description: Serum procalcitonin levels markedly elevated (>2 to 10 ng/mL, frequently exceeding 50 ng/mL in septic shock).

entities.name: Elevated ESR
entities.description: Marked acceleration of erythrocyte sedimentation rate (>80 to 100 mm/hr) in acute and subacute infection.

entities.name: Severe Hyperglycemia
entities.description: Admission plasma glucose significantly elevated (>200 to 450 mg/dL) unmasking diabetes or stress response.

entities.name: Elevated HbA1c
entities.description: Glycated hemoglobin exceeding 9% to 12%, proving chronic pre-existing hyperglycemia and neutrophil dysfunction.

entities.name: Acute Kidney Injury
entities.description: Sudden elevation of serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen secondary to septic acute tubular necrosis.

entities.name: Severe Lactic Acidosis
entities.description: Arterial lactate markedly elevated (>4.0 to 10.0 mmol/L) with severe high anion gap metabolic acidosis.

entities.name: Elevated Transaminases
entities.description: Mild to moderate elevations of AST and ALT (2 to 5 times upper limit of normal) reflecting microhepatic necrosis.

entities.name: Alkaline Phosphatase Elevation
entities.description: Disproportionate elevation of alkaline phosphatase (>2 to 4 times normal) indicating infiltrative microabscesses.

entities.name: Hyperbilirubinemia
entities.description: Elevated total and conjugated bilirubin resulting from sepsis-induced cholestasis and parenchymal injury.

entities.name: Markedly Elevated D-Dimer
entities.description: Plasma D-dimer markedly elevated (>5 to 20 µg/mL) with prolonged PT/INR indicating consumptive coagulopathy.

entities.name: Microscopic Pyuria
entities.description: Urinalysis demonstrating >20 to 50 leukocytes per high-power field reflecting urinary tract suppuration.

entities.name: Microscopic Hematuria
entities.description: Presence of red blood cells in urine sediment reflecting renal parenchymal necrosis or mucosal inflammation.

entities.name: CSF Neutrophilic Pleocytosis
entities.description: Cerebrospinal fluid showing moderate white cell pleocytosis (50 to 1,000 WBCs/µL) with elevated protein and normal-to-low glucose.

entities.name: Bipolar Safety-Pin Bacilli
entities.description: Direct Gram stain showing pleomorphic Gram-negative rods with characteristic bipolar 'safety-pin' staining appearance.

entities.name: Oxidase Positive Bacilli
entities.description: Rapid positive cytochrome oxidase enzymatic reaction on bacterial isolate colonies.

entities.name: Ashdown Agar Growth
entities.description: Characteristic deep purple, metallic sheen, wrinkled, rugose colonies growing on selective Ashdown agar after 48 hours.

entities.name: Pungent Earthy Odor
entities.description: Characteristic pungent, earthy, or musty aroma emitted by bacterial culture plates.

entities.name: Intrinsic Colistin Resistance
entities.description: Constitutive microbiological resistance to polymyxins (colistin and polymyxin B) on susceptibility testing.

entities.name: Aminoglycoside Resistance Profile
entities.description: Constitutive high-level resistance to gentamicin, tobramycin, and amikacin mediated by efflux pumps.

entities.name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
entities.description: Chronic metabolic disorder characterized by insulin resistance and hyperglycemia, impairing neutrophil oxidative burst.

entities.name: Hazardous Alcohol Use
entities.description: Chronic excessive alcohol consumption impairing alveolar macrophage activity and cellular immunity.

entities.name: Chronic Kidney Disease
entities.description: Underlying chronic renal impairment with uremia-associated immune dysfunction.

entities.name: Chronic Lung Disease
entities.description: Pre-existing structural pulmonary disorders such as COPD, cystic fibrosis, or bronchiectasis.

entities.name: Thalassemia Major
entities.description: Inherited hemoglobinopathy causing chronic hemolysis, iron overload, and macrophage dysfunction.

entities.name: Corticosteroid Immunosuppression
entities.description: Therapy with systemic corticosteroids or biologic immunosuppressants dampening cell-mediated immunity.

entities.name: Malignancy
entities.description: Underlying hematologic malignancies or active solid organ tumors undergoing cytotoxic therapy.

entities.name: Wet Muddy Soil
entities.description: Direct physical contact with tropical wet agricultural mud and soils containing saprophytic bacteria.

entities.name: Contaminated Surface Water
entities.description: Bathing, wading, swimming, or immersion in tropical freshwater rivers, canals, ponds, or floodwaters.

entities.name: Tropical Monsoon Season
entities.description: Annual seasonal heavy rains, high humidity, and rising water tables in tropical endemic regions.

entities.name: Severe Weather Cyclones
entities.description: Extreme tropical weather events including cyclones, typhoons, and hurricanes generating high winds and aerosols.

entities.name: Rice Paddy Farming
entities.description: Occupational immersion in waterlogged agricultural rice paddies without protective footwear.

entities.name: Percutaneous Inoculation
entities.description: Penetration of bacteria through minor lacerations, skin abrasions, insect bites, or puncture wounds.

entities.name: Aerosol Inhalation
entities.description: Direct respiratory tract inhalation of aerosolized bacterial particles in dust or water spray.

entities.name: Unchlorinated Drinking Water
entities.description: Consumption of untreated, unchlorinated rural bore water, well water, or contaminated domestic supplies.

entities.name: Southeast Asia Travel
entities.description: Residence in or travel history to hyperendemic regions of Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, or Singapore.

entities.name: Northern Australia Travel
entities.description: Travel to or residence in tropical Northern Territory (Top End), Kimberley, or northern Queensland.

entities.name: US Gulf Coast
entities.description: Environmental exposure within the newly recognized endemic environmental corridor along the US Gulf Coast.

entities.name: Laboratory Exposure Hazard
entities.description: Occupational aerosol or cutaneous exposure during benchtop handling of Burkholderia pseudomallei in microbiology laboratories.

entities.name: Incubation Period Days
entities.description: Acute incubation period following inoculation or exposure ranging from 1 to 21 days with a median of 9 days.

entities.name: Storm Inhalation Incubation
entities.description: Hyperacute onset of severe disease occurring within 24 to 48 hours after heavy storm inhalation or aspiration.

entities.name: Prolonged Latency Years
entities.description: Prolonged asymptomatic persistence of viable intracellular bacteria in tissues for months to decades.

entities.name: Vietnam Time-Bomb
entities.description: Clinical reactivation of dormant melioidosis occurring up to 62 years after departure from an endemic region.

entities.name: Zero Tropical Exposure
entities.description: Total lack of travel, residence, or contact with soil or water from tropical or subtropical endemic regions.

entities.name: Normal CRP Levels
entities.description: Normal serum C-reactive protein (<5 to 10 mg/L) in a patient presenting with acute systemic illness.

entities.name: Normal Procalcitonin
entities.description: Completely normal serum procalcitonin (<0.05 to 0.1 ng/mL) in a patient presenting with severe sepsis.

entities.name: Rapid Ceftriaxone Response
entities.description: Prompt clinical defervescence and cure within 48 to 72 hours of starting third-generation cephalosporins.

entities.name: Rapid Penicillin Response
entities.description: Rapid defervescence and clinical resolution on standard benzylpenicillin or ampicillin monotherapy.

entities.name: Aminoglycoside Monotherapy Response
entities.description: Clinical recovery and bacteriological clearance during gentamicin, tobramycin, or amikacin monotherapy.

entities.name: Vancomycin Monotherapy Response
entities.description: Successful clinical cure on vancomycin monotherapy.

entities.name: Ciprofloxacin Monotherapy Response
entities.description: Sustained clinical cure and eradication achieved with oral or IV ciprofloxacin monotherapy.

entities.name: Macrolide Monotherapy Response
entities.description: Prompt resolution of pneumonia on azithromycin or clarithromycin monotherapy.

entities.name: Rapid 48-Hour Defervescence
entities.description: Complete temperature normalization within 24 to 48 hours of starting targeted antimicrobial therapy.

entities.name: Acid-Fast Bacilli Smear
entities.description: Detection of acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen or auramine staining of sputum.

entities.name: Gram-Positive Diplococci
entities.description: Direct sputum or blood microscopy revealing lancet-shaped Gram-positive diplococci.

entities.name: Gram-Negative Diplococci
entities.description: Gram stain of CSF or blood showing intracellular kidney-bean-shaped Gram-negative diplococci.

entities.name: Prominent Hilar Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Prominent mediastinal and hilar lymph node enlargement accompanying cavitary lung disease.

entities.name: Eggshell Rim Calcification
entities.description: Peripheral eggshell calcification of visceral cystic lesions on plain radiographs or CT.

entities.name: Solitary Amebic Abscess
entities.description: Solitary large unilocular hepatic cavity with anchovy-paste aspirate and positive amoebic serology.

entities.name: Eschar Lesion Present
entities.description: Presence of a classic black necrotic tache noire eschar with regional lymphadenopathy.

entities.name: Severe Conjunctival Suffusion
entities.description: Bilateral non-purulent conjunctival injection with intense calf pain and deep jaundice.

entities.name: Rose Spots Rash
entities.description: Faint blanching salmon-pink macules on the trunk accompanied by step-ladder fever and bradycardia.

entities.name: Healthy Non-Exposed Host
entities.description: Young, immunocompetent host with normal glycemic status and zero outdoor environmental soil contact.

entities.name: Normal Blood Glucose
entities.description: Absence of diabetes, prediabetes, or metabolic risk factors combined with zero environmental exposure.

entities.name: Colistin Susceptible Isolate
entities.description: Clinical isolate showing in vitro susceptibility to colistin or polymyxin B.

entities.name: Tuberculosis
entities.description: Chronic mycobacterial infection causing upper lobe cavitary pneumonia, hemoptysis, and wasting.

entities.name: Leptospirosis
entities.description: Spirochetal zoonosis causing acute fever, conjunctival suffusion, jaundice, and renal failure after floodwater contact.

entities.name: Scrub Typhus
entities.description: Mite-borne rickettsial illness causing acute fever, eschar, sensorineural deafness, and rash.

entities.name: Typhoid Fever
entities.description: Systemic salmonella bacteremia causing step-ladder fever, relative bradycardia, rose spots, and splenomegaly.

entities.name: Staphylococcal Sepsis
entities.description: Gram-positive bacteremic sepsis causing multifocal soft-tissue abscesses, osteomyelitis, and septic shock.

entities.name: Klebsiella Pneumonia
entities.description: Severe Gram-negative necrotizing lobar pneumonia occurring frequently in diabetic and alcoholic patients.

entities.name: Bacterial Pneumonia
entities.description: Classic acute community-acquired pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae.

entities.name: Amebic Liver Abscess
entities.description: Invasive protozoan infection forming large unilocular hepatic cavity containing anchovy-paste pus.

entities.name: Pyogenic Liver Abscess
entities.description: Suppurative bacterial liver collection arising from ascending cholangitis or portal bacteremia.

entities.name: Malaria
entities.description: Mosquito-borne protozoan infection causing paroxysmal fevers, rigors, hemolytic anemia, and splenomegaly.

entities.name: Dengue
entities.description: Mosquito-borne flavivirus infection causing sudden high fever, retro-orbital pain, severe arthralgia, and plasma leakage.

entities.name: Acute Prostatitis
entities.description: Acute bacterial infection of the prostate gland typically caused by uropathogenic Escherichia coli.

entities.name: Bacterial Parotitis
entities.description: Acute suppurative parotid gland infection predominantly caused by Staphylococcus aureus.

entities.name: Listeriosis
entities.description: Foodborne intracellular bacterial infection causing rhombencephalitis, meningitis, and septicemia.

entities.name: Tuberculous Psoas Abscess
entities.description: Cold retroperitoneal abscess tracking from spinal tuberculosis (Pott disease) with vertebral bone destruction.

entities.name: Gonococcal Arthritis
entities.description: Disseminated Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection causing migratory tenosynovitis and septic arthritis.

entities.name: Histoplasmosis
entities.description: Endemic dimorphic fungal infection causing cavitary pneumonia, hepatosplenomegaly, and pancytopenia.

entities.name: Q Fever
entities.description: Zoonotic infection caused by Coxiella burnetii presenting with atypical pneumonia and culture-negative endocarditis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, acute fulminant septicemia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute fulminant septicemia is characterized by rapid hematogenous dissemination, refractory distributive shock, multi-organ failure, and mortality exceeding 40% to 50% without prompt bactericidal therapy.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, acute lobar pneumonia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute lobar pneumonia presents as primary inhalation or hematogenous consolidation involving single or multiple lobes, accompanied by high fevers and productive purulent sputum.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, subacute cavitary pneumonia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Subacute cavitary pneumonia closely mimics pulmonary tuberculosis with upper-lobe necrotizing parenchymal cavities, chronic cough, weight loss, and hemoptysis over weeks.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, suppurative parotitis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Suppurative parotitis is a hallmark pediatric presentation occurring in up to 30% to 40% of childhood melioidosis cases in Thailand and Cambodia, presenting with acute unilateral preauricular swelling.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, prostatic abscess
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Prostatic abscess occurs in 18% to 30% of adult males in endemic northern Australia, characteristically presenting with fever, perineal pain, urinary hesitancy, and acute urinary retention.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, splenic microabscesses
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Splenic microabscesses arise via hematogenous seeding and produce the classic multi-focal 'honeycomb' or 'Swiss-cheese' appearance on abdominal cross-sectional imaging.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, hepatic microabscesses
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Hepatic microabscesses develop during bacteremic dissemination, frequently coexisting with splenic lesions and causing right hypochondriac pain, fever, and elevated alkaline phosphatase.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, septic arthritis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Septic arthritis manifests as acute monoarthritis or oligoarthritis of the knee, hip, shoulder, or ankle with marked synovial effusion, erythema, and severe functional limitation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, acute osteomyelitis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute osteomyelitis involves long bones, pelvic girdle, vertebrae, or ribs, presenting with severe localized point tenderness, cortical osteolysis, and draining sinus tracts.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, brainstem encephalitis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Brainstem encephalitis characteristically presents with cerebellar ataxia, altered sensorium, autonomic instability, and multiple cranial nerve palsies.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, cranial nerve palsies
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Cranial nerve palsies occur frequently in neurological melioidosis, most commonly presenting with isolated unilateral lower motor neuron facial droop or ophthalmoparesis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, flaccid quadriparesis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Flaccid quadriparesis or paraparesis develops in neuromelioidosis secondary to acute necrotizing spinal cord myelitis or anterior horn cell infiltration.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, cutaneous pustules
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Cutaneous pustules emerge during bacteremic dissemination as crops of ecthyma gangrenosum-like pustules and furuncles with central necrotic ulceration.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, indolent skin ulcer
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Indolent skin ulcer represents primary localized cutaneous melioidosis, presenting with rolled violaceous edges, purulent discharge, and failure to heal on standard antibiotics.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, subcutaneous abscess
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Subcutaneous abscess manifests as single or multifocal fluctuant erythematous swellings across the trunk or extremities arising from direct inoculation or hematogenous seeding.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, suppurative lymphadenitis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Suppurative lymphadenitis presents with tender, warm, swollen regional lymph nodes draining primary inoculation sites that may progress to fluctuance and sinus tract formation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, pericardial effusion
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Pericardial effusion occurs via contiguous spread from mediastinal or pulmonary foci or hematogenous seeding, potentially progressing to cardiac tamponade.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, infective endocarditis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Infective endocarditis is a rare but catastrophic manifestation resulting in valvular destruction, persistent bacteremia, and septic embolic phenomena.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, mycotic aneurysm
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mycotic aneurysm characteristically involves the abdominal aorta or iliac arteries, presenting with pulsatile abdominal pain, fever, and high risk of catastrophic rupture.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, renal cortical abscess
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Renal cortical abscess manifests with high spiking fever, flank tenderness, pyuria, and potential extension into the retroperitoneum forming perinephric abscesses.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, epididymo-orchitis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Epididymo-orchitis presents with exquisite unilateral scrotal pain, erythema, testicular swelling, and abscess formation requiring surgical drainage or orchiectomy.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, psoas abscess
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Psoas abscess produces severe flank pain, fixed hip flexion contracture, and high fevers, often arising via direct extension from vertebral osteomyelitis or hematogenous spread.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, mediastinal abscess
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mediastinal abscess develops secondary to necrotizing pneumonia, suppurative mediastinal lymphadenitis, or thoracic surgical contamination, causing retrosternal pain and dysphagia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, pleural empyema
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Pleural empyema manifests as thick loculated exudative pleural fluid requiring tube thoracostomy or video-assisted thoracoscopic decortication alongside IV ceftazidime.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, cerebral abscess
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Cerebral abscess presents with focal neurological deficits, elevated intracranial pressure, intractable headaches, and seizures during bacteremic dissemination.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, necrotizing fasciitis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Necrotizing fasciitis presents with severe pain out of proportion to exam, skin bullae, ecchymosis, and rapid tissue necrosis requiring urgent surgical debridement.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, thyroid abscess
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Thyroid abscess presents with painful, warm, fluctuant anterior neck swelling, odynophagia, hoarseness, and fever resulting from hematogenous bacterial localization.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, corneal ulcer
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Corneal ulcer manifests as severe eye pain, conjunctival injection, corneal opacity, and hypopyon following direct splash inoculation of contaminated water or soil.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, adrenal abscess
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Adrenal abscess occurs during severe bacteremic seeding, causing adrenal hemorrhage, flank pain, and refractory hypotension due to acute corticosteroid insufficiency.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, pancreatic abscess
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Pancreatic abscess presents with severe persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back, vomiting, paralytic ileus, and high spiking fevers.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, peritonitis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Peritonitis manifests with diffuse abdominal guarding, rebound tenderness, rigidity, and cloudy peritoneal effluent in peritoneal dialysis patients.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, septic shock
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Septic shock manifests with profound vasodilation, hyperlactatemia, end-organ hypoperfusion, and an extreme systemic inflammatory response requiring high-dose vasopressor support.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, acute bronchitis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute bronchitis presents as a milder initial manifestation featuring persistent dry or productive cough, low-grade fever, and clear lung fields on plain chest radiographs.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, chronic melioidosis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Chronic melioidosis occurs in approximately 10% of patients, presenting with symptoms lasting over 2 months including fever, cachexia, and indolent cavitary pulmonary or visceral lesions.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, miliary melioidosis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Miliary melioidosis manifests with diffuse bilateral pulmonary micronodules on chest imaging and disseminated microabscesses in the liver, spleen, kidneys, and marrow.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, spinal epidural abscess
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Spinal epidural abscess presents with focal vertebral spine pain, radicular symptoms, lower extremity weakness, and sphincter dysfunction requiring emergent surgical decompression.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, pyomyositis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Pyomyositis manifests with localized muscular induration, severe localized pain, warmth, and subsequent fluctuance within large muscle groups such as quadriceps or iliopsoas.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, mesenteric lymphadenitis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Mesenteric lymphadenitis presents with right lower quadrant abdominal pain, guarding, nausea, and pyrexia mimicking acute appendicitis in young patients.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, deep neck abscess
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Deep neck abscess manifests with severe neck swelling, trismus, torticollis, odynophagia, and impending upper airway compromise.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, organ manifestation, clinical presentation, disseminated intravascular coagulation
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Disseminated intravascular coagulation manifests during fulminant septicemia with widespread petechiae, ecchymoses, oozing from venipuncture sites, and end-organ microvascular ischemia.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, preauricular parotid swelling
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Tense, tender, erythematous swelling over the preauricular region and angle of the jaw is the primary physical sign of acute suppurative parotitis.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, fluctuant parotid abscess
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Palpable fluctuance over the parotid bed with purulent expression from the intraoral Stensen duct is a pathognomonic physical hallmark of pediatric melioidosis in Southeast Asia.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, perineal tenderness
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Exquisite tenderness over the perineum between the scrotum and anus is a critical bedside indicator of underlying prostatic abscess.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, tender fluctuant prostate
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Digital rectal examination demonstrating an exquisitely tender, warm, and distinctly fluctuant prostatic lobe is a pathognomonic physical finding confirming prostatic abscess in adult males.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, acute urinary retention
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Inability to void accompanied by a tense, palpable suprapubic bladder mass reflects acute urethral compression secondary to severe prostatic abscess swelling.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, ecthyma-like necrotic pustules
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Crops of discrete cutaneous pustules surrounded by erythematous rings that rapidly evolve into ecthyma-like central necrosis are pathognomonic hallmarks of hematogenous bacteremia.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, violaceous undermined ulcer
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Inspection of skin lesions reveals a characteristic violaceous, purplish undermined border surrounding chronic indolent cutaneous ulcers at inoculation sites.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, high remittent fever
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] High remittent fever with spikes reaching 40°C is observed in acute pulmonary and bacteremic presentations, reflecting intense systemic pyrogen release.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, profound rigors
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Profound shaking rigors accompany temperature spikes, signaling active bacteremic showers and high circulating endotoxin levels.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, rules in, peripheral facial palsy
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Unilateral lower motor neuron facial palsy occurring in a febrile patient in an endemic zone is a hallmark physical anchor for brainstem neurologic melioidosis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, limb flaccidity
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Marked flaccidity with absent tendon reflexes in the extremities indicates acute lower motor neuron anterior horn cell involvement in neuromelioidosis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, truncal ataxia
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Truncal and gait ataxia on neurological exam reflects acute inflammatory involvement of cerebellar vermis and cerebellar peduncles in brainstem encephalitis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, abducens nerve palsy
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Abducens nerve palsy causes inward deviation of the eye and uncrossed horizontal diplopia due to focal pontine nuclear involvement.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, bulbar dysphagia
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Bulbar dysfunction presenting with profound dysphagia, dysarthria, and weak gag reflex results from medullary motor nuclei inflammation.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, nuchal rigidity
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Nuchal rigidity elicited on physical examination demonstrates meningeal irritation in patients presenting with melioidosis meningoencephalitis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, joint effusion
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Palpation reveals marked joint effusion, tense synovial swelling, erythema, and severe resting pain in joints affected by septic arthritis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, bony point tenderness
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Sharp, well-localized point tenderness over metaphyses of long bones or spinal spinous processes signals underlying osteomyelitis and subperiosteal abscess.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, positive psoas sign
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] A positive psoas sign on physical exam indicates retroperitoneal irritation and muscular inflammation caused by a tracking psoas abscess.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, costovertebral angle tenderness
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Sharp unilateral or bilateral costovertebral angle tenderness indicates acute renal parenchymal microabscesses or perinephric suppurative involvement.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, right hypochondriac tenderness
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Right hypochondriac tenderness with hepatomegaly and localized peritoneal guarding is elicited during physical examination of patients with hepatic microabscesses.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, left hypochondriac tenderness
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Exquisite tenderness over the left upper quadrant, sometimes with a palpable tender spleen or perisplenic friction rub, indicates acute splenic microabscesses.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, pleuritic friction rub
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Auscultation of the chest reveals a harsh, grating pleuritic friction rub caused by roughened fibrinous pleural surfaces in acute necrotizing pneumonia.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, tubular breath sounds
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Tubular bronchial breath sounds with egophony and whispering pectoriloquy over the upper lung fields indicate dense alveolar consolidation.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, tachypnea and retractions
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Tachypnea with prominent intercostal and sternal retractions signals severe pulmonary gas exchange failure and impending respiratory exhaustion.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, hyperdynamic vasodilation
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Examination reveals bounding pulses, widened pulse pressure, and warm flushed peripheries in the initial hyperdynamic distributive phase of melioidosis septic shock.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, mottled cold peripheries
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Cold clammy extremities with prolonged capillary refill and cutaneous mottling over the knees indicate severe systemic hypoperfusion and decompensated shock.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, petechial purpura
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Non-blanching petechiae and purpuric patches on the skin and conjunctiva indicate severe platelet consumption and microvascular thrombosis from DIC.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, bedside sign, physical examination, subcutaneous emphysema
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Palpable crepitation in subcutaneous soft tissues suggests rapidly dissecting necrotizing fasciitis or gas production in deep muscular compartments.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, radiology, bedside pocus, honeycomb splenic microabscesses
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Abdominal ultrasound or CT demonstrates multiple discrete, coalescing microabscesses scattered throughout the spleen creating the classic honeycomb pattern.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, radiology, bedside pocus, swiss-cheese hepatic microabscesses
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Cross-sectional imaging or bedside POCUS demonstrates multiple discrete hypoechoic microabscesses throughout the liver parenchyma resembling Swiss cheese.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, radiology, bedside pocus, prostatic fluid collections
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Transrectal or transabdominal ultrasound reveals discrete hypoechoic or anechoic fluid collections with posterior acoustic enhancement inside the prostate gland.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, radiology, bedside pocus, upper lobe cavitation
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Chest radiograph or CT reveals upper-lobe alveolar consolidation with rapid necrotizing cavitation closely mimicking secondary pulmonary tuberculosis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, radiology, bedside pocus, diffuse nodular infiltrates
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Chest imaging demonstrates diffuse bilateral poorly defined nodular opacities characteristic of hematogenous septic pulmonary emboli in bacteremic melioidosis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, radiology, bedside pocus, absence of hilar adenopathy
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Plain chest radiography characteristically demonstrates dense cavitary consolidation in the complete absence of hilar or mediastinal lymphadenopathy.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, radiology, bedside pocus, loculated pleural effusion
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Bedside thoracic ultrasound shows complex multi-loculated pleural fluid collections with thick septations and echogenic swirling debris confirming empyema.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, radiology, bedside pocus, pericardial fluid accumulation
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Focused bedside echocardiography demonstrates anechoic pericardial effusion with fibrinous bands and potential right ventricular diastolic collapse.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, radiology, bedside pocus, joint space distension
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Musculoskeletal ultrasound demonstrates marked hypoechoic joint effusion with power Doppler hypervascularity and synovial thickening in septic arthritis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, radiology, bedside pocus, subperiosteal fluid collection
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Ultrasound reveals an anechoic subperiosteal fluid collection stripping the periosteum over cortical bone irregularities, confirming acute osteomyelitis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, radiology, bedside pocus, t2 brainstem hyperintensity
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Cranial MRI demonstrates high signal intensity on T2-weighted and FLAIR images within the brainstem, pontine tegmentum, and cerebellar peduncles in neuromelioidosis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, radiology, bedside pocus, ring-enhancing cerebral lesions
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Contrast-enhanced cranial MRI reveals discrete nodular ring-enhancing lesions surrounded by finger-like vasogenic edema in cerebral melioidosis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, radiology, bedside pocus, psoas rim-enhancing fluid
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Contrast CT of the abdomen demonstrates a large hypodense collection with peripheral capsular enhancement within the psoas muscle belly.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, radiology, bedside pocus, mediastinal soft-tissue fullness
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Plain chest radiograph reveals mediastinal contour widening and retrosternal opacity reflecting acute suppurative mediastinitis or mediastinal abscess.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, marked neutrophilic leukocytosis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Complete blood count demonstrates marked neutrophilic leukocytosis (15,000 to 35,000/µL) reflecting profound bone marrow granulocytic stimulation.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, prominent toxic bandemia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Peripheral blood smear reveals prominent bandemia (>15%), toxic cytoplasmic granulations, and cytoplasmic vacuolation in circulating neutrophils.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, profound leukopenia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Severe leukopenia (<3,000/µL) with absolute neutropenia occurs in fulminant bacteremic septic shock and is associated with over 80% early mortality.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, severe thrombocytopenia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Rapid-onset severe thrombocytopenia develops during bacteremic dissemination secondary to platelet consumption and microvascular thrombi in DIC.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, massive crp elevation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Serum C-reactive protein is massively elevated (>150 to 300 mg/L) at hospital triage, confirming an intense invasive bacterial infection.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, marked procalcitonin elevation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Serum procalcitonin is markedly elevated (>2 to 10 ng/mL), providing strong discriminative evidence for invasive bacterial infection over viral or indolent mycobacterial disease.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, elevated esr
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Erythrocyte sedimentation rate is markedly accelerated (>80 to 100 mm/hr) reflecting intense hyperfibrinogenemia and systemic inflammation.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, severe hyperglycemia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Admission plasma glucose is frequently markedly elevated (>200 to 450 mg/dL), unmasking underlying uncontrolled type 2 diabetes mellitus.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, elevated hba1c
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) is frequently greater than 9% to 12% at triage, documenting chronic impaired glycemic control as the key host susceptibility.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, acute kidney injury
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Serum creatinine and BUN rise sharply at admission secondary to sepsis-induced renal hypoperfusion and acute tubular necrosis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, severe lactic acidosis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Arterial blood gas demonstrates severe lactic acidosis (lactate >4.0 mmol/L, pH <7.25) reflecting tissue hypoperfusion and anaerobic cellular metabolism.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, elevated transaminases
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Liver biochemistries show mild to moderate AST and ALT transaminitis secondary to hepatic microabscesses and ischemic hepatitis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, alkaline phosphatase elevation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Serum alkaline phosphatase is disproportionately elevated (>2 to 4 times normal) reflecting infiltrative intrahepatic granulomas and microabscesses.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, hyperbilirubinemia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Direct hyperbilirubinemia develops in severe bacteremic melioidosis due to cytokine-mediated intrahepatic canalicular cholestasis and hepatocellular injury.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, markedly elevated d-dimer
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Markedly elevated D-dimer alongside prolonged prothrombin time (PT/INR) and falling fibrinogen signals consumptive coagulopathy in septicemia.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, microscopic pyuria
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Urinalysis reveals prominent pyuria (>20-50 WBCs/HPF) resulting from direct prostatic abscess fistulization or renal microabscess shedding.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, microscopic hematuria
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Urinalysis demonstrates microscopic hematuria secondary to acute renal microabscesses, acute tubular injury, or severe cystourethritis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, csf neutrophilic pleocytosis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Lumbar puncture demonstrates moderate CSF pleocytosis (50-1,000 WBCs/µL) with mixed neutrophilic-mononuclear predominance and elevated protein in neuromelioidosis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, bipolar safety-pin bacilli
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Direct Gram stain of clinical specimens reveals pleomorphic Gram-negative rods with pathognomonic bipolar 'safety-pin' staining appearance.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, oxidase positive bacilli
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bacterial colonies yield a rapid positive oxidase test reaction, differentiating Burkholderia pseudomallei from oxidase-negative Enterobacteriaceae.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, ashdown agar growth
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Growth on Ashdown selective agar containing gentamicin yields characteristic wrinkled, purple, rugose colonies with a metallic sheen after 48-72 hours.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, pungent earthy odor
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bacterial culture plates emit a distinct, pungent, earthy or musty odor that provides an immediate diagnostic clue to trained laboratory personnel.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, intrinsic colistin resistance
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Disc diffusion or automated susceptibility testing demonstrates intrinsic high-level resistance to colistin and polymyxin B, an essential confirmatory marker.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, triage laboratory, aminoglycoside resistance profile
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] In vitro susceptibility testing reveals intrinsic resistance to gentamicin, tobramycin, and amikacin, preventing the use of standard Gram-negative sepsis coverage.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, host comorbidity, predisposition, type 2 diabetes mellitus
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Type 2 diabetes mellitus is the single strongest host risk factor, present in 40% to 60% of all melioidosis cases due to defective neutrophil oxidative burst and impaired phagocytosis.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, host comorbidity, predisposition, hazardous alcohol use
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Hazardous alcohol use is present in 15% to 30% of cases, suppressing alveolar macrophage phagocytic killing and predisposing to bacteremia and severe septic shock.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, host comorbidity, predisposition, chronic kidney disease
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Chronic kidney disease is an independent host risk factor present in 10% to 25% of patients, carrying heightened vulnerability to fatal bacteremic dissemination.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, host comorbidity, predisposition, chronic lung disease
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Chronic lung disease (COPD, bronchiectasis, cystic fibrosis) impairs local mucociliary clearance, facilitating pulmonary colonization following aerosolized bacterial inhalation.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, host comorbidity, predisposition, thalassemia major
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Thalassemia and chronic iron overload states promote rapid Burkholderia pseudomallei replication by supplying abundant essential free ferric iron in host tissues.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, host comorbidity, predisposition, corticosteroid immunosuppression
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Systemic corticosteroid therapy suppresses cell-mediated immunity and facilitates both acute primary infection and reactivation of latent dormant intracellular bacteria.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, host comorbidity, predisposition, malignancy
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Malignancy and cytotoxic chemotherapy predispose to severe bacteremic melioidosis by causing absolute neutropenia and profound mucosal barrier breakdown.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental risk, transmission route, wet muddy soil
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Direct contact with tropical wet soil and mud during agricultural or excavation activities is the primary environmental route of percutaneous bacterial inoculation.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental risk, transmission route, contaminated surface water
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Wading or immersion in contaminated surface freshwater, irrigation ditches, or post-monsoon floodwaters allows bacterial entry through open wounds or microabrasions.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental risk, transmission route, tropical monsoon season
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] The tropical monsoon season brings heavy precipitation that drives water tables upward, mobilizing saprophytic bacteria from deep soil to the surface and causing peak annual case spikes.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental risk, transmission route, severe weather cyclones
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Severe cyclones and typhoons aerosolize bacteria in airborne water droplets and dust, precipitating severe outbreaks of acute inhalation pneumonia.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental risk, transmission route, rice paddy farming
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Rice paddy farming involves hours of barefoot manual labor in waterlogged soil, constituting the highest occupational risk exposure for rural laborers in Southeast Asia.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental risk, transmission route, percutaneous inoculation
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Percutaneous inoculation occurs when broken skin, minor scratches, or puncture wounds come into direct contact with contaminated soil or surface water.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental risk, transmission route, aerosol inhalation
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Aerosol inhalation of fine soil dust or wind-whipped water droplets directly introduces bacteria into pulmonary alveoli, leading to acute fulminant pneumonia.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental risk, transmission route, unchlorinated drinking water
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Ingestion of unchlorinated domestic water supplies or contaminated borehole water allows bacterial translocation across oropharyngeal and gastrointestinal mucosa.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental risk, transmission route, southeast asia travel
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Residence or travel history to hyperendemic areas of Southeast Asia represents the classic geographic exposure establishing epidemiologic risk.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental risk, transmission route, northern australia travel
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Travel to or residence in tropical northern Australia carries high endemic risk, particularly during the wet season between November and April.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental risk, transmission route, us gulf coast
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Environmental exposure in the subtropical US Gulf Coast region (Mississippi, Louisiana, Texas) is recognized by the CDC as an established endemic reservoir.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental risk, transmission route, laboratory exposure hazard
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Accidental laboratory aerosol generation or sniffing culture plates of unidentified Gram-negative isolates poses a major occupational biosafety exposure hazard.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, temporal timeline, latency, incubation period days
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] The acute incubation period for melioidosis ranges from 1 to 21 days (median 9 days) following percutaneous or mucosal inoculation.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, temporal timeline, latency, storm inhalation incubation
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Following massive aerosol inhalation or near-drowning events during cyclones, the incubation period shortens dramatically to 24 to 48 hours.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, temporal timeline, latency, prolonged latency years
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Intracellular sequestration within macrophages enables prolonged asymptomatic latency persisting for months to decades prior to overt clinical reactivation.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, temporal timeline, latency, vietnam time-bomb
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Reactivation of dormant infection up to six decades after military or travel exposure in Southeast Asia earned melioidosis the moniker 'the Vietnam time-bomb'.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, zero tropical exposure
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Complete absence of travel, residence, or exposure to soil or freshwater from tropical or subtropical endemic zones virtually excludes Melioidosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, normal crp levels
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Normal serum CRP levels (<5 to 10 mg/L) in a febrile patient rules out invasive Melioidosis, which invariably elicits a massive systemic acute-phase response.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, normal procalcitonin
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Completely normal serum procalcitonin (<0.1 ng/mL) in a critically ill septic patient effectively excludes acute bacteremic Melioidosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, rapid ceftriaxone response
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Prompt clinical defervescence and resolution of pneumonia or sepsis on ceftriaxone or cefotaxime excludes Burkholderia pseudomallei due to intrinsic resistance.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, rapid penicillin response
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Rapid clinical recovery on standard penicillins or first-generation cephalosporins rules out Melioidosis due to constitutive PenA beta-lactamase production.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, aminoglycoside monotherapy response
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Clinical resolution during aminoglycoside monotherapy rules out Melioidosis because Burkholderia pseudomallei possesses intrinsic AmrAB-OprA efflux pumps.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, vancomycin monotherapy response
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Successful clinical recovery on vancomycin monotherapy rules out Melioidosis, as Burkholderia pseudomallei is an intrinsically glycopeptide-resistant Gram-negative bacillus.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, ciprofloxacin monotherapy response
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Sustained clinical cure on ciprofloxacin monotherapy makes Melioidosis highly improbable due to poor clinical efficacy and documented high failure rates.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, macrolide monotherapy response
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Rapid clinical resolution on macrolide monotherapy excludes Melioidosis, as Burkholderia pseudomallei is constitutively resistant to macrolides.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, rapid 48-hour defervescence
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Rapid defervescence within 48 hours of antimicrobial therapy rules out severe Melioidosis, as the median fever clearance time on optimal ceftazidime is 9 to 10 days.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, acid-fast bacilli smear
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Positive acid-fast bacilli on sputum smear microscopy identifies active Mycobacterium tuberculosis and excludes Burkholderia pseudomallei as the primary pathogen.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, gram-positive diplococci
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Direct microscopic visualization of Gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci confirms Streptococcus pneumoniae, excluding Gram-negative Burkholderia pseudomallei.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, gram-negative diplococci
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Direct microscopy demonstrating intracellular Gram-negative diplococci identifies Neisseria meningitidis, ruling out Burkholderia rods.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, prominent hilar lymphadenopathy
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Prominent hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy accompanying upper-lobe cavitation points strongly toward tuberculosis or fungal infection, as Melioidosis spares hilar nodes.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, eggshell rim calcification
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Peripheral eggshell calcification of visceral cystic lesions demonstrates echinococcal hydatid disease rather than acute suppurative melioidosis microabscesses.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, solitary amebic abscess
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Identification of a large solitary unilocular hepatic abscess with anchovy-paste aspirate and positive Entamoeba histolytica serology rules out Melioidosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, eschar lesion present
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of a pathognomonic necrotic black eschar with regional lymphadenopathy establishes scrub typhus or rickettsial infection, ruling out Melioidosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, severe conjunctival suffusion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Bilateral non-purulent conjunctival suffusion accompanied by intense calf tenderness and jaundice points directly to Leptospirosis rather than Melioidosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, rose spots rash
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Transient salmon-pink blanching rose spots on the abdomen with relative bradycardia indicates Salmonella enterica Typhi bacteremia, ruling out Melioidosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, healthy non-exposed host
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Acute septic presentation in a young immunocompetent individual with normal renal function and zero outdoor soil or water contact makes Melioidosis extraordinarily unlikely.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, normal blood glucose
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Normal fasting blood glucose and HbA1c in a patient lacking environmental soil or water exposure significantly reduces pre-test suspicion for Melioidosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, negative boundary, colistin susceptible isolate
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] In vitro susceptibility to colistin or polymyxin B definitively excludes Burkholderia pseudomallei, which is constitutively and universally resistant to polymyxins.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, tuberculosis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Tuberculosis presents with an insidious course over weeks to months, normal or mildly elevated WBC count, and acid-fast bacilli on smear; acute pulmonary melioidosis presents acutely over days with high leukocytosis (WBC >15,000/µL), toxic bandemia, and high procalcitonin.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, leptospirosis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Leptospirosis features non-purulent conjunctival suffusion, severe gastrocnemius calf tenderness, marked direct hyperbilirubinemia, and responds to ceftriaxone or penicillin; melioidosis presents with visceral microabscesses, prostatic suppuration, and intrinsic resistance to ceftriaxone.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, scrub typhus
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scrub typhus presents with a pathognomonic black necrotic eschar, sensory hearing loss, and rapid defervescence within 24 to 48 hours of doxycycline; melioidosis causes visceral or pulmonary microabscesses, marked leukocytosis, and prolonged fever clearance (9-10 days).

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, typhoid fever
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Typhoid fever exhibits relative bradycardia (Faget sign), step-ladder fever, leukopenia or eosinopenia, and faint rose spots; melioidosis presents with tachycardia, acute high leukocytosis with toxic bandemia, and honeycomb visceral microabscesses.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, staphylococcal sepsis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Staphylococcal sepsis presents with Gram-positive cocci in clusters, solitary large abscesses, and responsiveness to cefazolin or vancomycin; melioidosis is caused by Gram-negative bipolar bacilli, forms splenic honeycomb microabscesses, and fails vancomycin.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, klebsiella pneumonia
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Klebsiella pneumoniae produces currant-jelly sputum and responds to standard third-generation cephalosporins (ceftriaxone) and aminoglycosides; Burkholderia pseudomallei is intrinsically resistant to both ceftriaxone and aminoglycosides.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, bacterial pneumonia
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Typical bacterial pneumonia responds promptly within 48 to 72 hours to ampicillin, amoxicillin, or ceftriaxone; pulmonary melioidosis fails standard empirical beta-lactams and requires high-dose IV ceftazidime or meropenem.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, amebic liver abscess
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Amebic liver abscess typically forms a solitary large unilocular cavity with anchovy-paste aspirate and positive Entamoeba histolytica serology, responding to metronidazole; melioidosis causes multiple small microabscesses across the liver and spleen and fails metronidazole.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, pyogenic liver abscess
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Pyogenic liver abscess typically involves single or large multilocular collections caused by E. coli or K. pneumoniae that respond to ceftriaxone and metronidazole; melioidosis microabscesses feature concomitant splenic honeycomb lesions and require ceftazidime.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, malaria
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Malaria is diagnosed by intra-erythrocytic Plasmodium parasites on Giemsa blood smear and rapid antigen testing, lacking focal organ abscesses, cavitary pulmonary consolidation, or marked neutrophilic leukocytosis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, dengue
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Dengue features leukopenia with marked lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia with hemoconcentration, positive NS1 antigen, and defervescence by day 5 to 7, lacking purulent focal abscesses or marked neutrophilic leukocytosis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, acute prostatitis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Acute bacterial prostatitis caused by Enterobacteriaceae responds rapidly to fluoroquinolones or ceftriaxone without extensive parenchymal liquefaction; melioidosis causes large multilocular prostatic abscesses requiring prolonged IV ceftazidime and surgical drainage.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, bacterial parotitis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Staphylococcal parotitis occurs predominantly in dehydrated elderly patients, shows Gram-positive cocci on Gram stain, and responds to flucloxacillin; melioidosis parotitis occurs in healthy children in endemic regions and is caused by Gram-negative bipolar rods.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, listeriosis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Listeria monocytogenes causes rhombencephalitis in immunocompromised hosts but is a Gram-positive bacillus exquisitely sensitive to ampicillin and resistant to cephalosporins; Burkholderia pseudomallei is an ampicillin-resistant Gram-negative bacillus treated with ceftazidime.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, tuberculous psoas abscess
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Tuberculous psoas abscess presents indolently as a cold abscess with vertebral destruction and acid-fast bacilli; melioidosis psoas abscess presents acutely with high fevers, marked toxic leukocytosis, and viable Gram-negative bacilli in aspirated pus.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, gonococcal arthritis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Disseminated gonococcal arthritis presents with migratory tenosynovitis and vesiculopustular rash in young sexually active hosts, responding to ceftriaxone; melioidosis septic arthritis occurs in diabetic hosts, lacks migratory tenosynovitis, and fails ceftriaxone.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, histoplasmosis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Histoplasmosis is caused by dimorphic fungi identified on urine antigen assays or fungal stains, responding to amphotericin B and itraconazole; melioidosis is an aerobic Gram-negative bacterium growing on Ashdown selective agar.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, differential diagnosis, q fever
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Q fever presents following livestock exposure and is diagnosed by phase I/II serology, responding rapidly to doxycycline; melioidosis grows readily on blood and selective agar media and characteristically produces multiple visceral microabscesses.
